packageRules.description: Label every major so the failure alert can flag it as a BREAKING change needing a decision. Majors still auto-attempt (they fail CI + alert if they break) — deliberately NOT gated.
Autonomous loop: auto-merge all npm (dev+runtime, incl. major) on green. The real suite (unit+integration+e2e on a live stack) is the gate — a breaking bump fails CI and never merges.

Group ALL non-major npm updates into ONE PR. Every npm PR touches package-lock.json, so multiple open at once conflict the moment one merges (the queue clogs). One grouped PR = one lockfile change in flight = no sibling conflicts. Majors stay individual for blast-radius isolation.

Default for docker: manual (untested — monitoring, cloudflared, postgrest, meta). CI can't verify them yet; a weekly digest pings so they don't pile silently. Overridden below for candidate-tested images.
Docker majors: manual regardless — larger config surface than the Tier-1 candidate test covers.

Infra images WITH a candidate test (Tier-1 config-boot or Tier-2 DB-coupled): auto-merge patch/minor/digest, gated by the REQUIRED 'Tier-1 candidate boot' check (boots the candidate with real config/DB and probes health). Ordered AFTER the general docker rules so it wins (Renovate: later rule overrides). Majors excluded → stay manual via the rule above.
FROZEN stateful trio: auto-update is unsafe (migration/data coupling; storage has NO restore source, so 'roll back on failure' is impossible). Bumped only via a rehearsed restore.
